signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Options Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 154.07, holding below its daily SMA20 at 157.62, SMA50 at 159.69, and SMA200 at 158.41. The Fed at 3.75% maintains a +275bp policy rate advantage over the BoJ at 1.0%, with SOFR versus TONA generating a +264bp OIS carry advantage for the greenback. However, options demand displays an acute divergence, where the 25-delta risk reversal sits at -2.09, signaling strong put skew and heavy hedging against downside spot moves. CFTC Leveraged Funds trimmed short JPY exposure with a +58,042 contract WoW delta to -53,255 contracts, underscoring institutional repositioning ahead of the upcoming Bank of Japan policy decision. BoJ holds at 1.0%. Technical resistance stands at the SMA20 of 157.62, with fair-value models indicating the pair trades cheap at z=-2.69 relative to a 158.52 baseline. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, carry compression setup ahead of policy decisions. Catalyst: BoJ policy rate decision 18 Sep — rate hike expected. Risk: BoJ holds rates unchanged at 1.0%, prompting rapid short-covering back toward 157.60.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long Positioning vs Technical Resistance
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7155, hovering above its SMA20 at 0.7168, SMA50 at 0.7069, and SMA200 at 0.7003 daily moving averages. CFTC Leveraged Funds hold net long contracts of +48,379, placing speculative exposure at the 93rd percentile and z-score of +1.72 within its 52-week historical distribution. That positioning expansion stalled this week with Leveraged Funds delta recording -1,871 contracts WoW, signaling late-cycle fatigue among fast-money participants. The RBA at 4.35% versus the Fed at 3.75% provides a -60bp carry advantage supporting AUD, with AONIA over SOFR yielding a -73bp OIS spread. Options markets reflect caution as the 1-month 25-delta risk reversal prints a mild put skew of -0.67 despite the ongoing spot trend, while IV trades at 7.2% against HV30 of 6.0%, representing a +1.1% volatility risk premium. Resistance sits near the 0.7200 psychological handle, and a failure to sustain momentum leaves extended longs vulnerable to profit-taking. Trade bias: Neutral/range AUD/USD; positioning exhaustion constrains upside follow-through. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — market pricing rate hike. Risk: US retail sales or CPI prints miss heavily, triggering fresh institutional inflows into AUD carry.
evidence: RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75% — 60bp AUD carry advantage

signals.title: NZD/USD — Technical Breakdown and Dovish Repricing
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5786 after breaking through technical support at 0.5800 during the Asian session. Price remains positioned below the SMA20 at 0.5901, SMA50 at 0.5854, and SMA200 at 0.5857, confirming a broad bearish moving-average configuration across all standard horizons. New Zealand headline releases report explicit dovish policy rhetoric, accelerating selling pressure. The Fed at 3.75% maintains a +100bp policy rate spread over the RBNZ at 2.75%, backed by an 87bp SOFR over overnight OCR carry advantage. Leveraged funds hold net short exposure of -18,092 contracts, sitting at the 8th percentile of the 52-week range with a z-score of -1.40. Retail sentiment data retail sentiment shows a contrasting 74% long concentration, presenting an institutional-versus-retail divergence that reinforces downward momentum. Immediate technical resistance aligns at 0.5815, while the technical breakdown targets the next liquidity pocket at 0.5750. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD; rate disadvantage and technical breakdown favor ongoing downside. Catalyst: New Zealand Electronic Card Retail Sales release 22:45 UTC. Risk: US Dollar softens sharply following the FOMC meeting on 16 Sep, pushing spot back above 0.5855.
